name: How to Tell if a Foundation Crack Is Structural or Cosmetic in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: How do I know if a foundation crack in Los Angeles County is cosmetic or structural?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if a foundation crack in Los Angeles County is cosmetic or structural?

acceptedAnswer.text: The key difference is whether the crack is only in the finish material or whether it reflects movement in the foundation or framing. Cosmetic cracks are usually thin, stable, and limited to surface materials. Structural cracks are often wider, longer, directional, or paired with warning signs such as sloping floors, gaps at baseboards, sticking doors, or separation at corners. In Los Angeles County, soil expansion, settlement, hillside movement, and seismic forces can all contribute to structural changes. A contractor should inspect the crack location, measure any displacement, check the foundation perimeter, and compare inside and outside signs of movement. If the crack is widening or appears in multiple areas, the safest next step is a professional structural evaluation before patching, painting, or cosmetic repair.
acceptedAnswer.description: Hairline cracks in drywall or stucco are often cosmetic, but horizontal, stair-step, widening, or recurring cracks can indicate structural movement. A foundation repair contractor should check whether the crack pattern is active, whether doors and windows are sticking, and whether the slab or footing is moving. In Los Angeles County, soil movement and seismic activity can make structural cracks progress quickly.
